title: GPU id picking with a one-pixel render
purpose: Pick objects and instances in a three.js scene by rendering 24-bit ids as colours with a picking ShaderMaterial for only the pixel under the pointer (a view offset into a 1 x 1 target), reading the id back and restoring every material, the background and the camera. Use it for selection in big scenes.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: three.js passed in as THREE; the shaders use flat varyings (GLSL ES 3.00, WebGL 2). Only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.language: ECMAScript 2020 module; GLSL ES 3.00 through three.js ShaderMaterial

limits: Picking materials draw rest-pose geometry: skinned and morphed meshes are picked where their undeformed shape is. Transparent objects are picked as if opaque, alpha-tested cut-outs as full quads, and points, lines and sprites are hidden while picking. Each pick is one render of the scene (cheap per pixel but a full draw-call pass), so pick on pointer events, not every frame for many points. Ids above 16,777,215 do not fit. Multi-material meshes use the first material's side. Pixel coordinates are in renderer.getSize units. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Projection window offset (camera.setViewOffset) to render a single pixel
Flat varyings for exact integer ids
Integer to bytes with floor and mod in float32
